title.narrative: DT Institute-Building Inclusive Peace in Sudan (BIPS)
DT Institute-Building Inclusive Peace in Sudan (BIPS)

description.narrative:
1) Strengthening the capacity of community stakeholders, and youth in particular, to promote peace, and
2) Increasing engagement of communities, and youth in particular, in locally led peacebuilding activities that enhance trust, mutual understanding, and respect.

Building the capacity of youth, including young women, and community stakeholders such as local religious, tribal, and community leaders, herders and farmers, and others in Darfur, Blue Nile State, and South Kordofan to work together to identify and address community vulnerabilities to conflict through community action planning and small grants activities.

Bygga kapaciteten hos ungdomar, inklusive unga kvinnor, och samhällsaktörer som lokala religiösa, stam- och samhällsledare, herdar och bönder och andra i Darfur, Blue Nile State och South Kordofan att arbeta tillsammans för att identifiera och ta itu med samhällets sårbarheter för konflikt genom samhällsplanering och små bidragsaktiviteter.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
DTI's programme is up and running, staff has been hired and trained and DTI has finalized the organizational chart for the BIPS project. DT Institute has successfully been engaging with several partners across Sudan in various locations. The work of DTI has resulted in a roadmap with preliminary recommendations for its work in Sudan. DTIs work has also resulted in rapid assessment reports on the humanitarian situation in regions and/or states where DTI works. DTI also carried out assessments on conflict drivers in DTIs focus areas, which has included recommendations for programming. Despite the challenging operational environment, the war and Internet blackout, DT Institute collaborated with its partners to assist in developing their application submission skills to ensure quality. DTI:s work has thereafter resulted in releasing a call for applications for NGO:s to apply for small-grants.
The second RFP cycle attracted 44 potential applicants and resulted in 25 acceptable concept notes. Nine subgrants have been approved, with another eight pending. Support to local partners in developing their Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) plans, a MEL specialist has been added to the team. Operationally, the first payments for partners are being processed, with an emphasis on helping grantees to improve communication and standardizing documentation to enhance efficiency and clarity in processing their requests.
Approved grants are community focus on peacebuilding, psychosocial support, technology empowerment, and cultural documentation with project durations varying from four months to six months and two weeks. The pending grants worksheet includes a diverse set of projects aimed at addressing various community needs in Sudan. The key focus areas include peacebuilding, combating hate speech, trauma healing, youth advocacy, and cultural initiatives using music and arts.
While the program aims to ensure an equal number of grants across the three states, Blue Nile stands out with the highest number of approved grants, totaling five, and also leads with an additional three pending grants. In comparison, Darfur and South Kordofan each have two approved grants, but Darfur edges out South Kordofan in pending grants, with three compared to two. This difference is in part attributable to the greater instability in Darfur over the past several months.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
